rationale: iter-57: NAFNet (iter-56 base) + 3 trainable Wagner BF tails on the image-domain output. Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5804 (-1.02pp vs main baseline) but +0.81pp vs iter-56 bare NAFNet (0.5723). BF stacking IS substrate-independent: it adds real lift on mains wd=0 substrate, just smaller than on Agent As wd=1e-4 substrate (+1.22pp cumulative there). Not enough to beat mains alpha-scaling residual stack.
advice_for_others: The Wagner BF tail stacking is a substrate-independent +0.7-1.2pp mechanism. The substrate-dependence is in the BLOCK choice (NAFNet vs ResNet) and the AVERAGING (SWA / EMA): bare NAFNet is ~0.04pp worse than bare ResNet on mains wd=0; the BF stack lifts both by similar amounts but cannot close the gap on its own.
